name: RockOn Woo Variations Table
author: Vikas Sharma

sections.description:
RockOn Woo Variations Table turns WooCommerce’s variation dropdowns into a compact table, so shoppers can compare and order several products from one page instead of visiting each product in turn.

For wholesale and B2B stores, the bulk order grid lists every variation on its own row. Buyers type quantities, watch a running total, and add the whole order to the basket in one click, with no dropdowns at all.

Every feature is free.

Features

  • Shortcode [rovartable] and a “Variations Table” block.
  • Bulk order grid for wholesale buyers: every variation on its own row with a checkbox and quantity, a running total, and one button to add the whole order to the basket.
  • Instant filters above the table: a dropdown per attribute, “In stock only”, and search by name or SKU.
  • Admin page under WooCommerce → Variations Table: usage statistics, where every table is, a shortcode builder with live preview, store-wide settings and a reference.
  • Pick products by ID, category, tag, or product attribute.
  • Optional columns: image, title, SKU, attributes, price, stock, quantity, basket.
  • Live price, stock, SKU and image updates as options are chosen, with no page reload.
  • AJAX add to basket, including an optional “Add selected to basket” button for the whole table.
  • Works without JavaScript: every row falls back to a link to the product page.
  • Accessible markup: real table headers, labelled form controls, live-region status messages.
  • Responsive: whenever the table is wider than the space the theme gives it, it switches to a grid of product cards, so no column is ever hidden behind a sideways scroll.
  • Buttons pick up your theme’s own button style.
  • Respects the visitor’s light or dark colour scheme.
  • Fully translatable.

Performance

Variation data is embedded in the page so option matching happens instantly in the browser. Products with more variations than the limit (30 by default; change it under Settings or with the rwvt_ajax_variation_threshold filter) fall back to a single AJAX lookup, mirroring WooCommerce’s own behaviour. CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that show a table.

Admin page

Everything lives under WooCommerce → Variations Table, for anyone who can manage WooCommerce (store managers included).

  • Overview — the last 30 days at a glance (adds from tables, units added, paid orders and revenue that came from tables, each compared with the 30 days before), every page, post, template or pattern that holds a table with links to edit or view it, and a check of WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP versions.
  • Shortcode builder — pick products by name, or categories and tags, choose a layout, columns, filters and options, and copy the shortcode. A live preview shows the table as you go. The shortcode only names what differs from your defaults.
  • Settings — store-wide defaults that every table and block follows unless it sets its own: “basket” or “cart” wording, layout, filters, hiding out-of-stock items, linking product names, grid paging and whether grid products start closed. Also the number of variations sent with the page, usage statistics on or off, and whether deleting the plugin deletes its data.
  • Help — a quick start, the full shortcode reference and the developer hooks.

Usage statistics and privacy

When statistics are on (the default), the plugin keeps daily totals for 90 days: how many add-to-basket actions came from a table, how many items and units they added, and how many paid orders and how much revenue included them. Revenue is each order line’s share that was added from a table, after discounts and before tax; refunds are not taken off. No personal data is stored: no customer, IP address or order details, only the totals. A table add is marked on the basket line, copied to the order line as hidden meta (_rwvt_qty) at checkout, and counted once when the order is paid. Statistics can be switched off or deleted under Settings.

Shortcode

Basic use:

[rovartable id="12,34,56"]

Choosing products

  • id — comma separated product IDs, rendered in the order given.
  • category — comma separated product category slugs.
  • tag — comma separated product tag slugs.
  • attribute + terms — a product attribute slug and its term slugs, e.g. attribute="colour" terms="red,blue".
  • exclude — product IDs to leave out.
  • categories_exc — category slugs to leave out.
  • limit — maximum number of products (0 = no limit).
  • orderby — date, title, menu_order, ID, rand or modified. Default date.

  • order — ASC or DESC. Default DESC.

    id takes priority: when it is set, the category, tag and attribute filters are ignored.

Controlling the table

  • columns — comma separated, in display order. Available: image, title, sku, attributes, price, stock, quantity, button. Default title,attributes,price,stock,quantity,button.
  • thead — custom header labels, comma separated, replacing the defaults in order.
  • caption — a visible caption above the table.
  • class — extra CSS classes on the wrapper.
  • link_titles — yes (default) or no.
  • add_all — yes to show an “Add selected to basket” button. Default no.
  • disabled — yes renders a read-only table with no dropdowns, quantity fields or basket buttons. Default no.

Bulk order grid

[rovartable layout="grid" category="workwear" per_page="10"]
  • layout — table (default) shows one row per product, with a dropdown for each option. grid shows one row per variation, grouped under a header row for each product.
  • per_page — grid only: products per page. A product’s variations always stay together on one page. 0 (default) lists every product on one page.
  • collapsed — grid only: yes (default) starts each product closed, so the grid reads as a list of products; click a product’s header row to open it. no starts them open.

In the grid, typing a quantity ticks the row, and ticking a row fills in its minimum quantity. The checkbox in the header selects every available row on the current page, and the one beside each product name selects all of that product’s variations and opens the product. A summary bar counts the selected items, units and subtotal, and stays at the bottom of the screen while anything is selected.

“Add selected to basket” adds everything in one request. If an item cannot be added, for example because there is not enough stock, its row stays ticked and shows the reason, and the rest are still added; a closed product opens to show it. Out-of-stock variations are listed but cannot be ticked. A variation that accepts any value for an attribute shows a dropdown for just that attribute.

Grid columns default to attributes,sku,price,stock,quantity, because the product name and image already appear in each header row. Add image to show each variation’s own image, or button for a basket button on every row.

Filters

[rovartable layout="grid" category="workwear" filters="all"]
  • filters — controls to show above the table, comma separated: attribute slugs such as colour or size (a dropdown each, listing only values the table’s products have), attributes for every attribute, search (matches product name, SKU and option names) and stock (“In stock only”). all shows every one. Default: none.
  • hide_out_of_stock — yes hides out-of-stock items when the page loads. With the stock filter shown, its box starts ticked and shoppers can untick it. Default no.

Filtering is instant and needs no page reload. A count shows how many rows match, with a “Clear filters” link.

In the grid, filters work on variations: “Size: L” lists only the L variations, products without a size are hidden, and a variation that accepts any value for an attribute matches every value. Closed products open while you search or filter by an option and fold away again when the filters are cleared. “Select all” only selects rows that match, and anything already ticked stays ticked when a filter hides it.

In the dropdown table, filters work on whole products: a product is listed if it offers the chosen value. The chosen value is also filled into each listed product’s dropdown, so “Size: L” leaves every product set to L, but a dropdown the shopper has already changed is left alone.

Examples

[rovartable id="12,34" thead="Product,Colour,Size,Price,Stock,Qty,Basket"]

[rovartable category="t-shirts" limit="10" orderby="title" order="ASC" columns="image,title,sku,attributes,price,quantity,button" add_all="yes"]

[rovartable attribute="colour" terms="red" caption="Everything in red"]<h3>Hooks</h3>

Filters:

  • rwvt_product_ids — the resolved product ID list for a table.
  • rwvt_table_columns — the resolved column definitions.
  • rwvt_table_filters — the controls shown in the filter bar.
  • rwvt_render_custom_column — render a custom column’s cell.
  • rwvt_no_products_message — the output when a table matches nothing.
  • rwvt_script_settings — the configuration handed to the front-end script.
  • rwvt_ajax_variation_threshold — inline variation payload cut-off.
  • rwvt_grid_max_rows — the most variation rows one bulk order grid renders (default 1000).
  • rwvt_bulk_max_items — the most items one “Add selected to basket” request may add (default 200).

Upgrading from version 6

Your existing shortcodes keep working. [rovartable id="12,34"] and [rovartable id="12,34" thead="Title,Colour,Size,Basket"] render the same columns they always did.

A shortcode that supplies thead keeps the version 6 column set (title, one column per attribute, then basket), because thead labels are positional and adding the new columns would shift every label onto the wrong one. To take the new Price, Stock and Qty columns, name them explicitly:

[rovartable id="12,34" columns="title,attributes,price,stock,quantity,button" thead="Product,Colour,Cost,Availability,Amount,Basket"]

Shortcodes without thead gain the new columns automatically.

Two behaviour changes to be aware of

  • disabled was accepted but never did anything in version 6. It now renders a read-only table. If you had disabled on a shortcode, remove it unless you want that.
  • categories_exc was also accepted and ignored. It now genuinely excludes those categories.

Custom CSS

These version 6 hooks are unchanged: .ron-woo-table-section, tbody.row-hover, tr.row-2, .even, .odd, td.value, td.column-5, select.user_vote.

These are gone, because the markup they belonged to was invalid or buggy: div.ro-loader-*, input#ron-att-name-*, select#ron-attr-*, and a#add-cart-*. The basket control is now button.rwvt-add-to-cart, and each cell carries data-column so it can be targeted reliably.

Custom PHP

ron_woo_variations_table(), `ron_woo_variable_add_to_cart()` and `ron_woo_find_matching_product_variation()` still exist as deprecated wrappers, so template customisations will not fatal. They log a deprecation notice when `WP_DEBUG` is on and will be removed in a future major release; move to `do_shortcode( '[rovartable ...]' )`.

Custom JavaScript

The check_choosed_var AJAX action and the global getVarData() function have been removed. The replacement endpoints require a nonce. If you wrote custom scripts against them, they need updating.

Requirements

Version 7 needs WordPress 6.4+, PHP 7.4+ and WooCommerce 8.0+. On older setups WordPress will not offer the update, so those sites simply stay on version 6 rather than breaking.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the rockon-woo-variations-table folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it through Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu.
  3. Add the [rovartable] shortcode to any post or page, or insert the “Variations Table” block.

WooCommerce must be installed and active.
sections.faq:
Does this work with simple products?

Yes. Simple products are shown as ordinary rows with a working add to basket button. Where a column does not apply to a product, the cell shows a dash so the table stays aligned.

What if two products have different attributes?

The header is the union of every attribute in the table. A product that does not use one of them shows a dash in that column.

Can shoppers deep link to a preselected option?

Yes. Append WooCommerce’s usual attribute parameters, for example ?attribute_pa_colour=blue, and matching dropdowns are preselected on load.

Does it work without JavaScript?

The table renders in full, and each row shows a link to the product page instead of the basket button. Switching to cards needs JavaScript, so without it a table too wide for its space scrolls sideways instead.

Why does my table show as cards on a desktop screen?

Many themes keep page content in a narrow column, often around 600–700px, and a table with several option columns needs more room than that. Rather than hide the price and basket columns behind a sideways scroll, the plugin switches to cards. To show it as a table, give it more room: choose “Wide width” on the block’s alignment toolbar, or add class="alignwide" to the shortcode on a block theme. Showing fewer columns also helps, for example columns="title,attributes,price,button".

How do I change the number of variations sent to the browser?

Set “Variations sent with the page” under WooCommerce → Variations Table → Settings (30 by default), or filter rwvt_ajax_variation_threshold per product. Products above the limit use a single AJAX request per selection instead.

Can the buttons say “cart” instead of “basket”?

Yes. Choose “Cart” under WooCommerce → Variations Table → Settings → Wording. Every button and message the tables show changes. Sites in other languages keep their translation’s own word.

What happens to my settings if I delete the plugin?

They are kept, along with the usage statistics, so reinstalling picks up where you left off. To remove them, tick “Delete these settings and the statistics when the plugin is deleted” under Settings before deleting the plugin.

Is it compatible with HPOS and block checkout?

Yes, compatibility is declared for high performance order storage, cart and checkout blocks, and the product block editor.
sections.changelog:
7.1.0

New

  • Bulk order grid (layout="grid"): one row per variation, grouped under each product, with checkboxes, quantities, “select all”, a summary bar with a running subtotal, and one “Add selected to basket” request that adds everything it can and explains any row it cannot.
  • Grid products can start closed (collapsed), and paging keeps each product’s variations together (per_page).
  • Instant filters above the table (filters, hide_out_of_stock): a dropdown per attribute, “In stock only”, and search by name or SKU, in both layouts.
  • Admin page under WooCommerce → Variations Table: an overview with usage statistics, where every table is and a status check; a shortcode builder with live preview; store-wide settings; and a reference.
  • “Basket” or “cart” wording, chosen in Settings.
  • Usage statistics: daily totals of adds, orders and revenue from tables, stored on your own site with no personal data. They can be switched off or deleted.
  • A “View product” link under a basket button that cannot be used yet, so a greyed-out button is never a dead end.
  • Block settings for layout, products per page, starting closed and filters.
  • New filters: rwvt_table_filters, rwvt_grid_max_rows and rwvt_bulk_max_items.

Improved

  • Refreshed look: tidier type, styled dropdowns and quantity fields, buttons that follow your theme’s button style, and a basket icon that matches the button text.
  • Tables switch to cards whenever they are wider than the space they are given, not only on phones, and on wide screens the cards sit side by side.
  • The basket button on variable products says “Add to basket” instead of WooCommerce’s “Select options”.
  • Price ranges no longer wrap with the dash on a line of its own.

Fixes

  • WooCommerce error messages, such as “not enough stock”, no longer show HTML codes like ".

7.0.0

7.0.0

A full rewrite. Please review your existing shortcodes after updating.

Security

  • Both AJAX endpoints now require a nonce and reject unverified requests.
  • All request input is sanitised and validated; product and variation IDs are checked for existence, status and parentage.
  • All output is escaped. Fixes a stored XSS vector through the thead attribute.
  • Responses use wp_send_json_*() instead of echoing raw text.
  • Added an ABSPATH guard and directory index files.

Compatibility

  • Replaced every deprecated WooCommerce 2.x/3.x call: $product->id, array access on attributes, and get_matching_variation() are gone.
  • Products are loaded with wc_get_product() instead of new WC_Product_Variable().
  • Declared compatibility with HPOS, cart and checkout blocks, and the product block editor.
  • Fixed PHP 8.1+ deprecation notices.
  • The plugin now degrades to an admin notice when WooCommerce is inactive, instead of a fatal error.
  • Added Requires at least, Requires PHP, WC requires at least and WC tested up to headers.

Fixes

  • Table headers and row cells now always line up, even when products have different attributes.
  • Removed an invalid <div> between <table> and <thead>.
  • The basket control is a real <button disabled>, so an unavailable combination can no longer be added.
  • DOM IDs are unique per table instance, fixing collisions between products and repeated shortcodes.
  • Add to basket links no longer depend on the current page’s permalink, so they work on archives and shop pages.
  • An empty or invalid id now shows “No products found.” instead of a blank row.
  • Implemented categories_exc, which was previously accepted and ignored.
  • Removed the unused preselected-value code and reimplemented it properly as query string deep linking.
  • Each product is now loaded once per table instead of twice.

Front end

  • CSS and JS are enqueued only on pages that render a table, and no longer printed inline in wp_head on every request.
  • Rewritten in dependency-free vanilla JavaScript, so it no longer breaks on themes that do not load jQuery.
  • No inline event handlers, so the plugin works under a strict Content Security Policy.
  • Assets carry a version string for cache busting.

New

  • “Variations Table” block with a live editor preview.
  • Image, SKU, price, stock and quantity columns.
  • AJAX add to basket with cart fragment refresh.
  • “Add selected to basket” bulk action.
  • Product selection by category, tag or attribute.
  • Read-only table mode.
  • Responsive card layout on small screens, and full keyboard and screen reader support.
  • Surface-aware colours: neutral tones are alpha based so they sit correctly on any theme background, and the table measures the theme’s actual background rather than trusting the operating system’s dark mode preference. A light-only theme viewed on a machine set to dark mode keeps readable colours.
  • Complete internationalisation with a .pot template.

6.0

  • Earlier releases.
